disclosure: Original pattern text; fictional examples where stated. No AI generation in this prototype. Control references are candidate links, not a compliance assessment.

evidence.author: Demo editor
evidence.source: Original fictional interview, reviewed public summary
evidence.text: Fictional incident: the handoff included a short receipt listing the change, signals to watch, the next owner, and an acknowledgement. A long email had previously gone unread. Completeness competed with attention. The receipt reduced ambiguity in two rehearsed handoffs, with the cost of maintaining a concise summary. It helps across shifts; it fails when the receiving team lacks authority or cannot acknowledge. Candidate evidence: acknowledged handoff record; do not treat acknowledgement as proof of effectiveness.

pattern.author: Demo editor
pattern.benefits: Ambiguity is visible before the sender leaves.
pattern.boundaries: Assumption: the receiver can act. Seek a counterexample from an unstaffed shift. Acknowledgement is not evidence of effectiveness.
pattern.context: Work passes between shifts or operating teams.
pattern.controls: Candidate operational control: continuity of responsibility. Possible evidence: dated handoff receipt.
pattern.costs: A summary must be maintained and acknowledged.
pattern.exceptions: An acknowledgement cannot confer missing authority.
pattern.name: An acknowledged handoff
pattern.problem: A sender mistakes a sent message for shared understanding.
pattern.resulting_context: The receiving team has accepted the next action.
pattern.solution: Send a short receipt naming the change, watch signals, and next owner; obtain an explicit acknowledgement.

review.note: Reviewed original fictional summaries and original pattern wording; no real participant information. CC0-1.0 applies to the demo content.
